title: India's 'AI 100' Names 100 Agency Leaders Reshaping Brands With AI
excerpt: Indian Startup Times has published "The AI 100: Agency Leaders Redefining Brands with AI," an editorial list recognizing 100 agency and marketing leaders across India who are bringing artificial intelligence into brand building — from creative technologists and prompt-engineering-certified tech leads to veteran media planners.
body:
• Indian Startup Times has published "The AI 100: Agency Leaders Redefining Brands with AI," an editorial list recognizing 100 agency and marketing professionals across India who are shaping how brands adopt artificial intelligence.
  • The list spans the global holding companies — WPP, Publicis Groupe, dentsu, Omnicom and Havas — alongside a long roster of independent agencies, and covers creative, media, technology, data and communications roles.
  • The profiles reflect AI's move from experiment to operations: technology leaders with prompt-engineering credentials, a "Director of Growth and AI-Digital Marketing," and creative-tech executives running AI-led campaigns.
  • The publisher stresses this is editorial recognition, not a ranking — the order of names implies no hierarchy, and inclusion is not an endorsement of any individual or AI implementation.

Indian Startup Times published "The AI 100: Agency Leaders Redefining Brands with AI" this week, a 100-person editorial list recognizing agency and marketing leaders across India who are driving artificial intelligence into brand building. The feature, researched and edited by Muskan Dengra and Vanshika Tayal, is built from publicly available information — company websites, LinkedIn profiles, professional biographies, industry publications and media coverage.

The editors frame it as AI's move from "an emerging technology" to "an increasingly integrated part of agency operations" — making leadership, in their words, "central to navigating this transformation responsibly and effectively."

Who made the list

The 100 names are drawn from every layer of India's agency ecosystem. Global networks are heavily represented: WPP agencies (Mindshare, Ogilvy, VML, WPP Media, Grey, GroupM), Publicis Groupe (Leo Burnett, Digitas India, Publicis Sapient, Publicis Global Delivery, Starcom), dentsu India, Omnicom Advertising, and Havas's PivotRoots. Independents appear throughout — Hashtag Orange, GOZOOP Group, Schbang, BC Web Wise, Grapes, Techmagnate, #ARM Worldwide, AGENCY09, Magnon Group, Madison World and Edelman.

A few profiles show how directly AI has entered agency job descriptions. Mohammedullah Shaikh, who leads technology services at Digitas India, carries a certification in advanced prompt engineering. Sanjay Kumar is Director of Growth and AI-Digital Marketing at Grapes, embedding AI into search, content and performance strategy. Vaishali Mange, Vice President of Creative Tech at Ogilvy India, has worked on AI-focused campaigns for Cadbury 5 Star. Sujay Ghosh, Executive Vice President and Business Partner at Omnicom Advertising, publicly describes himself as an AI evangelist.

Experience runs deep across the roster. Hemant Kshirsagar brings more than 18 years across fintech and consulting to his role leading dentsu India's financial services and technology business. Rohit Eric D'Souza has spent around 16 years in media planning and buying at Mindshare. Sanil Jadhav of LS Digital Group cites more than ₹1,000 crore in media exposure across 100-plus Indian brands.

What the list signals

The AI 100 is the latest in a run of list-style editorial projects from Indian Startup Times mapping the marketing-technology ecosystem — earlier entries include a "Top 50 Leaders in Advertising Technology, Platforms, Data & AI" and a "Search 100" of digital search leaders.

The substance lies in the job titles. A decade ago, agency recognition lists would have been dominated by creative directors and client-service heads. Product managers for influencer platforms, creative technologists, digital delivery leads and growth heads with explicit AI mandates now sit alongside traditional creative and client-service leaders. Prompt engineering appearing as a listed professional credential is one of the clearest signals that AI capability has become a hiring and promotion criterion, not a side project.

"The future of brand building will not be defined by technology alone, but by how effectively leadership combines innovation with creativity, context, and human understanding."

— Indian Startup Times, "The AI 100" conclusion

India's marketing-tech talent pipeline

The list also doubles as a reminder of how much global marketing machinery runs through India. Publicis Global Delivery's India teams support the group's global media operations, and several of the named leaders sit in delivery and operations roles serving international clients. For the Indian diaspora working in marketing and advertising abroad — from New York to Singapore — the roster maps counterparts back home operating at the same scale.

It lands in a year of widening Indian recognition in AI more broadly. TIME's fourth edition of TIME100 AI, published August 27, named ten Indians and people of Indian origin among the 100 most influential people in AI, including Sarvam AI co-founder Vivek Raghavan, Adalat AI co-founder Utkarsh Saxena, IBM CEO Arvind Krishna, Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra and Caltech professor Anima Anandkumar, as YourStory reported.

What's next

Indian Startup Times says the selection is not exhaustive, not a ranking, and not an endorsement of any individual, organization or AI implementation. What it does offer is a snapshot of a profession mid-reinvention. Watch whether the AI 100 becomes an annual fixture — and whether the agencies named can turn AI credentials into measurable brand outcomes as client expectations harden.
